topic: sub:11|Time and location|Time and time differences

parts.latex:
Sydney is 10 hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC $+10$) and New York is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC $-5$).

Tony travels from Sydney to New York. His plane leaves Sydney at 8:20 pm on Wednesday local time and flies non-stop to New York.

The flight takes 20 hours and 24 minutes.

What time and day is it in New York when the plane lands?

solutions.latex:
Sydney is ahead of New York by
$$10 - (-5) = 15 \text{ hours}$$
Add the flight time to the departure time (Sydney time):
$$8{:}20 \text{ pm Wednesday} + 20\text{ h }24\text{ min} = 4{:}44 \text{ pm Thursday}$$
Subtract the time difference to get New York time:
$$4{:}44 \text{ pm} - 15 \text{ hours} = 1{:}44 \text{ am}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{it is } 1{:}44 \text{ am Thursday in New York}$$
criteria: Finds the time in Sydney when the plane lands in New York, or equivalent merit
Finds the time difference between Sydney and New York, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Sakura will travel from Sydney (UTC $+10$) to Rio de Janeiro (UTC $-3$).

The flight from Sydney to Rio de Janeiro will take 20 hours.

The flight will arrive in Rio de Janeiro at 3 pm on Wednesday 20 July.

On what day and at what time will Sakura leave Sydney?

solutions.latex:
Sydney is 13 hours ahead of Rio (UTC $+10$ and UTC $-3$).

Rio arrival time minus flight time:

$$3\text{ pm}-20\text{ hours}=7\text{ pm Tuesday 19 July (Rio time)}$$

Add the time difference of 13 hours:

$$7\text{ pm}+13\text{ hours}=8\text{ am Wednesday 20 July}$$

Alternative method: convert the arrival to Sydney time first.

$$3\text{ pm}+13\text{ hours}=4\text{ am Thursday 21 July}$$

$$4\text{ am}-20\text{ hours}=8\text{ am Wednesday 20 July}$$

Sakura leaves Sydney at 8 am on Wednesday 20 July.
criteria: Provides 7 pm Tuesday or 4 am Thursday, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
The Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) of Auckland is $+12$ hours and the UTC of Chicago is $-5$ hours.

When the time in Chicago is 2 pm, Thursday, what is the time in Auckland?

solutions.latex:
The time difference is the difference between the UTC offsets.
$$12 - (-5) = 17 \text{ hours}$$
Auckland is 17 hours ahead of Chicago.

Add 17 hours to 2 pm Thursday. Adding 10 hours gives 12 am Friday, and 7 more hours gives 7 am Friday.

The time in Auckland is 7 am, Friday, option D.

parts.latex:
Diego flew from Sydney to Hong Kong. Diego departed Sydney at 10:15 pm Coordinated Universal Time (UTC +10) on Wednesday and travelled via Singapore.

The flight from Sydney to Singapore took 7 hours 50 minutes.

The time between arriving in Singapore and departing from Singapore was 2 hours and 15 minutes.

The flight from Singapore to Hong Kong took 3 hours 40 minutes.

Singapore and Hong Kong both operate on UTC +8.

What time and day was it when Diego arrived in Hong Kong?

solutions.latex:
Hong Kong is UTC $+8$ and Sydney is UTC $+10$, so the time difference is
$$10 - 8 = 2 \text{ hours}$$
Total travel time:
$$7\text{ h }50\text{ min} + 2\text{ h }15\text{ min} + 3\text{ h }40\text{ min} = 13\text{ h }45\text{ min}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Arrival} &= 10{:}15\text{ pm} + 13\text{ h }45\text{ min} - 2\text{ h} \\ &= 10{:}15\text{ pm} + 11\text{ h }45\text{ min} \\ &= 10{:}00\text{ am Thursday} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Diego arrived at 10:00 am Thursday, Hong Kong local time}$$
criteria: Finds the travel time, or equivalent merit
Finds the time difference, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A football game is being played in Quito (UTC $-5$) starting at 3:40 pm on Tuesday.

What is the time in Sydney (UTC $+10$) when the game starts in Quito?

solutions.latex:
Convert the Quito time to UTC, then to Sydney time.

Quito is UTC $-5$, so UTC is 5 hours ahead of Quito:
$$3{:}40\text{ pm} + 5 \text{ h} = 8{:}40 \text{ pm Tuesday (UTC)}$$
Sydney is UTC $+10$, so add 10 hours:
$$8{:}40\text{ pm} + 10 \text{ h} = 6{:}40 \text{ am Wednesday}$$
The difference between the two places is 15 hours.

Hence the correct option is D.

meta.self_check: Time difference 15 h added to 3:40 pm Tuesday.

parts.latex: If it is 2:30 pm on Tuesday in Montreal (UTC $-$ 4), what time and day is it in Perth (UTC $+$ 8)?

solutions.latex:
Perth is ahead of Montreal by
$$8 + 4 = 12 \text{ hours}$$
Adding 12 hours to 2:30 pm Tuesday:
$$\therefore\ \text{2:30 am Wednesday}$$
criteria: Finds the time difference of 12 hours, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Maximilian is in Athens, which is two hours ahead of the Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). Dominic is in New York, which is five hours behind UTC.

Dominic is going to fly from New York to Athens. His flight will leave on Wednesday at 9am, New York time, and will take 11 hours.

What day and time will it be in Athens when he arrives?

solutions.latex:
Athens is 2 hours ahead of UTC and New York is 5 hours behind UTC, so the time difference is
$$2 - (-5) = 7 \text{ hours}$$
Arrival in New York time: $9\text{ am} + 11\text{ h} = 8\text{ pm}$ Wednesday.

Add the time difference to get Athens time.

$\therefore$ Dominic arrives in Athens at $3$ am Thursday.
criteria: Finds the time difference and the New York arrival time, or equivalent merit
Finds the time difference, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Sydney is 10 hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC + 10) and New York is 5 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC $-5$).

Tony travels from Sydney to New York. His plane leaves Sydney at 8:20 pm on Wednesday local time and flies non-stop to New York.

The flight takes 20 hours and 24 minutes.

What time and day is it in New York when the plane lands?

solutions.latex:
The time difference is
$$10-(-5)=15 \text{ hours}$$
Add the flight time to the departure time (Sydney time): $8{:}20 \text{ pm Wednesday} + 20 \text{ h } 24 \text{ min} = 4{:}44 \text{ pm Thursday}$.

New York is 15 hours behind Sydney, so subtract 15 hours: $4{:}44 \text{ pm} - 15 \text{ h} = 1{:}44 \text{ am}$.

$$\therefore\ \text{it is } 1{:}44 \text{ am Thursday in New York}$$
criteria: Finds the time in Sydney when the plane lands in New York, or equivalent merit
Finds the time difference between Sydney and New York, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Sandy is on holiday in San Francisco and wants to stream a Matilda's World Cup match which is played in Sydney on Monday $31^{\text{st}}$ July and starts at 3:00 pm.

San Francisco is located at UTC $-8$ and Sydney at UTC $+10$.

San Francisco is subject to daylight saving in July and August, but Sydney is not.

At what time and date in San Francisco should Sandy start streaming the match?

solutions.latex:
Convert the Sydney start time to UTC. Sydney is UTC $+10$, so subtract 10 hours.
$$\begin{aligned} 3{:}00 \text{ pm Monday} &= 15{:}00 \text{ Monday (Sydney)} \\ \text{UTC} &= 15{:}00-10{:}00 = 5{:}00 \text{ am Monday} \end{aligned}$$
San Francisco is UTC $-8$, but daylight saving makes it UTC $-7$ in July.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{San Francisco} &= 5{:}00 \text{ am Monday}-7 \text{ h} \\ &= 10{:}00 \text{ pm Sunday} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Sandy should start streaming at } 10{:}00 \text{ pm on Sunday } 30^{\text{th}} \text{ July}$$
criteria: Finds the UTC time ($5{:}00$ am Monday) and the correct San Francisco offset, or equivalent merit
Finds the UTC time, or applies the correct time difference of $17$ hours with the wrong direction, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Time difference Sydney to SF in July is 17 h; 15:00 - 17:00 = 22:00 previous day.

parts.latex:
Roger’s flight itinerary is shown below. It details the departure and arrival times of the flights on his journey from Sydney to London. Only local times are shown in the table, and all departures and arrivals occur on the same Sunday.

\exfigure{850_q28_1}

Roger knows that Sydney is 7 hours ahead of Dubai, and that Dubai is 3 hours ahead of London.

How long did Roger spend flying?

solutions.latex:
Sydney is 7 hours ahead of Dubai, so when the flight leaves Sydney it is 23:00 on Saturday in Dubai.

Landing at 13:20 on Sunday means the first flight took 14 hours 20 minutes.

Dubai is 3 hours ahead of London, so when the flight leaves Dubai it is 13:05 on Sunday in London.

Landing at 20:00 on Sunday means the second flight took 6 hours 55 minutes.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Total flight time}&=14\text{ hr }20\text{ min}+6\text{ hr }55\text{ min}\\&=21\text{ hr }15\text{ min}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the flight time of ONE of the flights, or equivalent merit
Finds the time AND day in Dubai when Roger departs Sydney, or equivalent merit
Finds the time in Dubai when Roger departs Sydney, or equivalent merit

850_q28_1.notes: Flight itinerary, transcribed. 'Depart' and 'Arrive' each span two columns. The top-left cell is empty and has no border on the paper. Header words are bold italic or bold, as on the paper. Rules 6b, 8.

parts.latex:
A movie marathon started at 8:15 pm. At the end of the marathon an audience member noted that the time on their watch in 24-hour time was 1345 the following day.

How long did the movie marathon last?

solutions.latex:
Use the degrees, minutes and seconds button on the calculator.
$$\begin{aligned} t &= 24^\circ + 13^\circ 45' - 20^\circ 15' \\ &= 17^\circ 30' \end{aligned}$$
That is, 17 hours 30 minutes, so the answer is C.

parts.latex: Melissa flies out of Brisbane at 11am on Sunday and arrives in Brussels 26 hours later. If Brussels is 9 hours behind Brisbane, find the time in Brussels when Melissa arrives?

solutions.latex:
First find the arrival time in Brisbane time.
$$11\text{ am Sunday}+26\text{ hours}=1\text{ pm Monday}$$
Brussels is 9 hours behind Brisbane, so subtract 9 hours.
$$1\text{ pm Monday}-9\text{ hours}=4\text{ am Monday}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Melissa arrives at 4 am Monday in Brussels}$$

parts.latex:
The Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) of Hawaii is $-10$ hours.

When it is 9 pm Wednesday in Hawaii, it is 12:30 pm Thursday in India.

What is the UTC of India?

solutions.latex:
Hawaii is UTC$-10$, so UTC time is $10$ hours ahead of Hawaii time.
$$9\text{ pm Wednesday} + 10 \text{ h} = 7\text{ am Thursday (UTC)}$$
India's time is $12:30$ pm Thursday, so India is ahead of UTC by
$$12:30 - 7:00 = 5\text{ h }30\text{ min}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the UTC of India is } +5{:}30 \text{ (UTC } +5.5)$$
criteria: Finds the time in UTC (7 am Thursday) or the time difference between Hawaii and India (15.5 hours), or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Difference Hawaii to India 15.5 h; minus 10 gives 5.5.

parts.latex: A plane takes 12 hours to fly from Adelaide (UTC $+9.5$) to Cape Town in South Africa (UTC $+2$). If Shaunna leaves Adelaide at 10:00 am, what is the local time when she arrives in Cape Town?

solutions.latex:
The time difference is
$$9.5 - 2 = 7.5 \text{ hours}$$
Adelaide is ahead of Cape Town, so go back 7.5 hours from 10:00 am, then add 12 hours of flying time.
$$10\text{:}00\text{ am} - 7.5 \text{ h} + 12 \text{ h} = 2\text{:}30\text{ pm}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{It is 2:30 pm on the same day.}$$
criteria: Finds the correct time difference, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Elizabeth lives in New York, USA (UTC –5) and Margaret lives in Sydney, NSW (UTC +10). Margaret makes a call to Elizabeth at 12:30 pm on Monday 24th February. February is a month when NSW has daylight saving time and the USA doesn't.

What it the time in New York when Elizabeth receives the call?

solutions.latex:
Sydney is ahead of New York by $10-(-5)=15$ hours, plus $1$ hour for daylight saving, so $16$ hours.

New York time is $16$ hours earlier than $12{:}30$ pm Monday.

$$12{:}30\text{ pm Monday}-16\text{ h}=8{:}30\text{ pm Sunday 23rd February}$$

Hence the correct option is the one giving $8{:}30$ pm Sunday 23rd February.

6802.stem:
Coordinated Universal Times for the following cities are:

Sydney (NSW): UTC +10

Brisbane (QLD): UTC +10

Auckland (NZ): UTC +12

Between October and March, NSW and New Zealand have daylight saving of +1 hour.

Queensland (QLD) does \underline{not} have daylight saving.

parts.latex: In May, when it is Sunday 1:00 am in Auckland (NZ), what is the local time and day in Sydney (NSW)?
In January, Alison wanted to call her family in Auckland to wish them a Happy New Year. If it is 10 am in Brisbane when Alison calls, what is the time in Auckland?

solutions.latex:
In May there is no daylight saving, so Sydney is UTC $+10$ and Auckland is UTC $+12$.

Sydney is 2 hours behind Auckland.

$$\text{Sydney time} = \text{Sunday } 1{:}00\text{ am} - 2\text{ h}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Saturday, } 11{:}00\text{ pm}$$

In January daylight saving applies in New Zealand, so Auckland is UTC $+13$. Queensland has none, so Brisbane is UTC $+10$.

Auckland is 3 hours ahead of Brisbane.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Auckland time} &= 10\text{ am} + 3\text{ hrs} \\ &= 1\text{ pm} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
$P$ is 7 hours behind place $R$. Landing restrictions at place $R$ require that planes cannot land or take-off from 11 pm to 6 am. A flight from $P$ to $R$ is expected to take 10.5 hours.

At what times of the day does a plane need to leave from $P$ to be allowed to land at $R$?

solutions.latex:
When it is a time at $P$, the time at $R$ is found by adding the flight time and the 7 hour difference.

$$\text{Time at } P + 10.5 + 7 = \text{Time at } R$$
$5{:}30\text{ am}$ at $P$ is $11\text{ pm}$ at $R$.

$12{:}30\text{ pm}$ at $P$ is $6\text{ am}$ at $R$.

So planes need to leave $P$ from $12{:}30\text{ pm}$ to $5{:}30\text{ am}$, or equivalently, outside the interval from $5{:}30\text{ am}$ to $12{:}30\text{ pm}$.

parts.latex: Sara decides to take the 15:46 express train from Paramatta to Strathfield instead of the 15:59 all stations train. How much time does she save?

On Monday, George takes the 15:45 train from Harris Park and stops at Clyde for a coffee. He then takes the 16:05 train and gets off at Strathfield and walks 53 minutes to his apartment in Concord.

Work out the total duration of his journey from Harris Park to Concord and the time he reaches the apartment in 24-hour time.

solutions.latex:
Express: $12$ min.

All stations: $18$ min.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time saved} &= 18 - 12 \\ &= 6 \text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correctly calculates any one journey time

solutions.latex:
Harris Park $15{:}45$ to Strathfield $16{:}17$, then a $53$ minute walk.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total time} &= 15 + 17 + 53 \\ &= 85 \text{ min} \\ &= 1 \text{ hr } 25 \text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{He reaches the apartment at } 17{:}10$$

parts.latex:
Belinda lives in Dubbo, NSW, which is in the Eastern Standard Time zone of UTC + 10. Felicity lives in Denver, Colorado, which has the time zone of UTC $-7$.

If Belinda makes a call to Felicity at 7:30 am on Friday 5th July (Dubbo time), what will be the local time in Denver when Felicity receives the call?

solutions.latex:
Dubbo is UTC $+10$ and Denver is UTC $-7$, so Denver is $17$ hours behind Dubbo.
$$7{:}30\text{ am Friday} - 17\text{ h} = 2{:}30\text{ pm Thursday}$$
This is option D.
